extracted.intended_audience: Mathematicians and programmers producing mathematical figures with MetaPost / m3D (MetaPost users)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing high-quality mathematical figures (2D and 3D, implicit curves, parametrized curves, graphs on manifolds) using MetaPost and the m3D/m3Dplain libraries; includes code examples and macros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit arrows/breadths/radii/spreads to 10pt Computer Modern
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows, breadths, radii and spreads are intended to fit 10 points' Computer Modern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design sizes (arrowheads, line breadths, radii, spread parameters) so they visually match 10pt Computer Modern type; this is an explicit sizing target mentioned for the dynkin/mp input/style so drawn diagrams harmonize with TeX typeset text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use m3Dplain format and standard 3D settings
rubrics_metrics.description: This picture has been created quite rapidly with my m3Dplain format: input m3Dplain.mp; ObjectColor:=0.75white; Resolution:=1mm; ProjectionSystem(linear); unit:=1cm;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the m3Dplain include and the shown global parameters (ObjectColor, Resolution, ProjectionSystem, unit) as a standard starting configuration for 3D drawings. The example demonstrates how to set projection system and scale units to ensure consistent rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling technique: blankdotlabel to avoid filled bounding boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: vardef blankdotlabel@#(expr t,loc) = save lab_; picture lab_; lab_=thelabel@#(t,loc); unfill bbox lab_; dotlabel@#(t,loc); enddef;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a macro that computes the label picture, un-fills its bounding box (unfill bbox lab_) and then applies dotlabel to place the label. This prevents filled label boxes from obscuring underlying drawing elements — a practical anti-pattern fix for labels with background fills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reusable objects (UseObject) for complex 3D shapes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encapsulate common 3D constructions (revolution solids, spheres, etc.) as reusable objects and invoke them with UseObject(...). This modular approach simplifies complex scenes and promotes reuse across figures (example: UseObject(revolution,Origin,Origin,unit,p) used twice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit curves: solve f(x,y)=c numerically (use implicit.mp)
rubrics_metrics.description: What is more interesting is drawing implicit curves, i.e., curves defined by an equation like (x,y) in R^2 such that f(x,y)=c ... Strangely, numerical methods for solving such problems are never described anywhere. ... The equation x^3+y^3-3xy=0 whose solutions form an elliptic curve. The program is implicit.mp and has been written late in a monday evening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drawing implicit curves in MetaPost, use numerical methods to find points on f(x,y)=c; the author provides implicit.mp as an example. Note the remark that such numerical techniques are rarely documented, so reusing tested code (implicit.mp) or implementing robust numerical solvers is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametric/functional curves via path definitions and MetaPost expressions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define parametrized or piecewise-smooth paths using MetaPost path syntax and arithmetic expressions (e.g., sqrt5, sqrt2). Use direction specifiers ({down}) and smooth joins to control curve shape; this is the standard way to build parametrized graphical elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use TeX labels via btex/etex and labeled arrow/axis conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: drawarrow proj(unit,0,0)..proj(4unit,0,0); label.lft(btex $x$ etex,proj(4unit,0,0)); drawarrow proj(0,unit,0)..proj(0,4unit,0); label.bot(btex $y$ etex,proj(0,4unit,0)); ... dotlabel.lft(btex $A$ etex, proj(unit,0,0));
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use btex ... etex to typeset mathematical labels with TeX and place them with label.* and dotlabel.* placement specifiers. Combine drawarrow for axes and consistent label placement to produce publication-quality annotated figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draw graphs on manifolds (e.g., torus) with m3D
rubrics_metrics.description: Pol Vanhaecke asked me if I was able to draw some graph on a torus. ... This picture has been made with the m3D programs, also it was one of the first time I attempted to draw curves on manifolds with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For embeddings that cannot be drawn planar (e.g., K5), use manifold-aware m3D tools to represent curves on surfaces like a torus. The author demonstrates embedding a complete graph on the torus as an example of when manifold representation is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer MetaPost/m3D for high-quality mathematical pictures over hand drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: Previous samples are quite old now, but this doesn't mean that I'm no longer programming simple figures with MetaPost ... Paul Broussous seems to share with me some kind of love for mathematical pictures ... Every time he attempts to draw a picture with some mathematical software I won't name ... I try to do the same with my own tools (MetaPost of course).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MetaPost (and m3D) to create reproducible, high-quality mathematical graphics rather than relying on hand-drawn sketches. The examples emphasize programmatic figure creation for precision and publication quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and reuse: copyleft / postcard request policy
rubrics_metrics.description: HTML's texts or graphics are free of any copyright, they are copyleft. TeX programs are also copyleft but one can send a postcard. MetaPost programs have just a feel-free-to-send-me-a-postcard licence. MetaFont programs have the standard LaTeX licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reusing material from this site, respect the author's stated licensing: textual and graphical content is copyleft (free), TeX and MetaPost code are effectively copyleft but the author requests a postcard as a courtesy, and MetaFont code follows standard LaTeX licensing. Treat these as the author's distribution and attribution preferences.
